source.author: verg
source.text: Toto namque fremunt condensae litore puppes Signaque ferre iubent; retinet longaevus haruspex fata canens, O Maeoniae delecta iuventus, flos veterum virtusque virum, quos iustus in hostem fert dolor et merita accendit Mezentius ira, nulli fas Italo tantam subiungere gentem:
source.text_original: Toto namque fremunt condensae litore puppes / Signaque ferre iubent; retinet longaevus haruspex / fata canens, 'O Maeoniae delecta iuventus, / flos veterum virtusque virum, quos iustus in hostem / fert dolor et merita accendit Mezentius ira, / nulli fas Italo tantam subiungere gentem: /
source.text_english: For all along the shore the crowded ships are roaring, and they order the standards to be borne; but the aged seer, singing of destiny, holds them back: O chosen youth of Maeonia, flower and strength of men of old, whom righteous anger against the enemy drives on and whom Mezentius kindles with deserved wrath, it is not lawful for any Italian to bring so great a people under subjection.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_original: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi / progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi / exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras / terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens / instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_english: but there was no rest for his mind, nor for his fearful brother, because of the offspring and the threats of the gods; for seers proclaim that this man will be the king’s destruction, and the dreadful warnings repeat themselves through the altars of the sacrificial beasts: over and above the man himself looms a great renown and a valor not pleasing to the tyrant.
